extracted.intended_audience: users and contributors of Mathlib and Lean (students, developers, library maintainers)
extracted.subtask_description: An index and overview of the documentation available for Mathlib and Lean, including documentation types (tutorials, how‑tos, references, explanations) and concrete style, naming, and library notes that govern how to write code, docs, and contributions for Mathlib.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorials
rubrics_metrics.description: Tutorials are lessons that take you by the hand through a series of steps to complete a project of some kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Natural Numbers Game, Glimpse of Lean, Mathematics in Lean, Mechanics of Proof; intended as stepwise, guided learning resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: How-to guides
rubrics_metrics.description: How-to guides take you through the steps required to solve a real-world problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: project setup guides, 'How to use calc', 'How to speed up a Mathlib file', and contributor setup instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference guides are complete technical descriptions of the machinery and how to operate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Lean 4 tactic cheatsheet, Mathlib API documentation, Lean Language Reference; intended as comprehensive, lookup-style documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations clarify and illuminate a particular topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: common pitfalls, conceptual introductions, and pedagogical notes such as 'What is a quotient?'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathlib naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines how Mathlib names declarations in a systematic way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative guidance used to choose consistent declaration names across the library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library style guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines how to format code to contribute to Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative style rules for Lean/Mathlib code formatting; used when authoring contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation style guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines how to write documentation for your contributions to Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative rules on prose, examples, placement, and format for docs included with code contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pull request title and description conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the writing style of text in a pull request for contributions to Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative conventions for crafting PR titles and descriptions to be clear and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contribute to Mathlib
rubrics_metrics.description: How-to guide for contributors to Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps and expectations for contributing (development workflow, testing, review process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Git Guide for Mathlib4 Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: How-to guide for making effective use of Git, focussed on contributing to Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive git workflows and branch management practices recommended for contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pull Request Review Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write a good review for pull requests to Mathlib. For everyone, not just members of the maintainer team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on what to check in a PR, how to give constructive feedback, and reviewer responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting up linting and testing for your Lean project
rubrics_metrics.description: How to add a linting and testing framework to a math project in Lean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive steps to integrate linters and tests so contributions meet repository quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project setup: globally shared mathlib installation
rubrics_metrics.description: A trick to not download different Mathlib installations for each of your Lean projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical project configuration guidance to ensure consistent dependencies across projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project setup: following stable releases
rubrics_metrics.description: A trick to specify only stable releases of your dependencies in the Lakefile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure to pin dependencies to stable Mathlib releases to improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project setup: using local development version of a dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: A trick to use local copies of a repository for development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developer workflow recommending how to test changes across local forks before PRing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathlib API documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete listing of all definitions and theorems included with Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical API reference for declarations; used as authoritative source for available lemmas and defs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathlib Documentation: Tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation on tactics included with Mathlib, including a complete index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference and usage examples for tactics shipped in Mathlib; consult when choosing tactics or writing tactic docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean 4 tactic cheatsheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheatsheet for the most common tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick reference; marked incomplete in the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean Language Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete description of the features included in core Lean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authoritative language specification for Lean; consult for language semantics and core features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean Glossary
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations of terminology one might encounter in the Lean community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology reference to ensure consistent use of terms in documentation and code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [custom simps projection]
rubrics_metrics.description: How to register projections for the @[simps] attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instructions for configuring simps projections for better generated lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [reducible non-instances]
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions that cannot be instances should be made reducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule recommending reducibility for definitions that should not be declared as instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [implicit instance arguments]
rubrics_metrics.description: Some places prefer implicit {} brackets for typeclass arguments instead of typical instance [] brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when to use implicit curly-brace arguments for typeclasses to improve readability or inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [lower instance priority]
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating an instance that always applies, give it a lower priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule to avoid high-priority instances that shadow more appropriate ones and slow inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [instance argument order]
rubrics_metrics.description: A trick to speed up typeclass instance synthesis by putting more specific goals first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical ordering guidance for instance arguments to improve typeclass search performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [SetLike Aesop ruleset]
rubrics_metrics.description: How to add rules about SetLike membership to Aesop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for registering Aesop rules concerning SetLike to improve automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [no_index around OfNat.ofNat]
rubrics_metrics.description: Write ofNat(n) in lemmas instead of OfNat.ofNat n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style recommendation to avoid index noise in lemma statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [coercion into rings]
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set up coercions from a concrete structure like ℕ to an arbitrary ring R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design pattern for setting up numeric coercions to improve generality of lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [RCLike instance]
rubrics_metrics.description: An instance creating a goal [RCLike ?m] is okay since there are only two choices, ℝ or ℂ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance clarifying when a seemingly ambiguous instance is acceptable because the domain is small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [fact non-instances]
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not declare any global instances of the Fact typeclass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative rule preventing global Fact instances to avoid unwanted instance resolution behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [decidable namespace]
rubrics_metrics.description: The Decidable namespace contains theorems that avoid the use of the Law of Excluded Middle by using Decidable instances instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions about placement and intent of the Decidable namespace to help choosing the right lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [decidable arguments]
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Decidable hypothesis is not needed for the type signature of a theorem or lemma, use classical instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to avoid adding decidable hypotheses to statements when they are not part of the type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [slow-failing instance priority]
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that would be slow to fail to apply should have a lower priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance guideline to set lower priorities for instances that are expensive to attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [foundational algebra order theory]
rubrics_metrics.description: Batteries sets up the algebraic and order theoretic properties of Nat and Int; Mathlib replaces this with a typeclass-based system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory note on design choice and migration away from battery-style globals to typeclasses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [continuity lemma statement]
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write more useful continuity lemmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on formulating continuity statements to be maximally usable in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [comp_of_eq lemmas]
rubrics_metrics.description: How to avoid elaboration problems when writing the continuity of a composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice to prevent elaboration errors in composed continuity lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [IMO geometry formalization conventions]
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions for formalizing geometry problems from the IMO as part of Mathlib's Archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific stylistic and structural conventions for archive formalizations of contest geometry problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [change elaboration strategy with `by apply`]
rubrics_metrics.description: A trick to elaborate a term and its type in a different order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactic-writing / proof-authoring trick to influence elaboration order when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [pointwise nat action]
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of natural numbers or integers on sets takes precedence over pointwise actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disambiguation guidance to ensure consistent interpretation of actions on sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [Design choices about smooth algebraic structures]
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathlib's design choices about smooth algebraic structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level design guidance for how smooth algebraic structures are represented in the library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [Manifold type tags]
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains why ModelProd and ModelPi exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale for specific design choices in the manifold API.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [non-Archimedean non-instances]
rubrics_metrics.description: Why non-Archimedean subgroup basis lemmas cannot be instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation of technical limitations that motivate non-instance design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [range copy pattern]
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of a morphism f is defined using Set.range if possible, not map ⊤ f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred pattern for defining images to avoid unnecessary complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [continuous functional calculus]
rubrics_metrics.description: Design overview of the continuous functional calculus in Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectural documentation for a major component of the analysis library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [specialised high priority simp lemma]
rubrics_metrics.description: When not to un-@[simp] a lemma in favour of a more powerful version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on managing simp lemma priorities and avoiding removing useful specialized simp lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [out-param inheritance]
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on the interaction of typeclass inheritance and outParam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical warning and constraints to consider when designing typeclass hierarchies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [lower cancel priority]
rubrics_metrics.description: Inheritance from cancellative algebraic structures gets a lower priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority-setting guidance for algebraic inheritance to optimize instance resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [forgetful inheritance]
rubrics_metrics.description: Design pattern for typeclass inheritance where we include all fields, even if they can be inferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern recommendation to make derived structures explicit for clarity and robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [norm_num lemma function equality]
rubrics_metrics.description: Why lemmas for the norm_num tactic use a parameter f and hypothesis f = HAdd.add instead of writing +.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation of a design choice in lemma formulation to aid the norm_num tactic's operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [hom simp lemma priority]
rubrics_metrics.description: Widely applicable @[simp] lemmas should receive mid priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule of thumb for assigning simp priorities to widely useful lemmas to balance automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [category theory universes]
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patterns for ordering the universe levels in category theory declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions for universe ordering to keep categorical declarations consistent and usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [operator precedence of big operators]
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of operator precedence for ∏ and ∑ operators in Mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convention for operator precedence to ensure consistent parsing of big operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library note [bundled maps over different rings]
rubrics_metrics.description: A design trick for when bundled maps have stronger properties if certain typeclass assumptions are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design pattern to exploit stronger properties conditionally via bundled maps and typeclasses.
